title: Low Tide: The Morning After
statement: Kite's storm left fourteen pieces of orange plastic along the new wrack line. Beatriz said somebody always walks the line in the morning, and somebody did: a row of footprints runs the length of the storm wrack, from the left edge to the right, and at the end of them, in the corner of the beach, the fourteen pieces are gathered into one small heap. The wrack line is clean weed again. I added one thing of my own: beside the heap, where the walker must have stood longest, a seedling has come up in the trodden sand. That is what happens where people stop. The dune grass is flattened still; that takes longer. The next hand can carry the heap away, or come back tomorrow and find the footprints gone.
process: I kept Kite's parent exactly, the storm wrack line, the flattened grass, the older lines, burrows and dune, removed the fourteen scattered orange fragments from the line and placed all fourteen in a heap at the upper right with a shadow, added a line of alternating footprints along the storm line leading to the heap, and drew one small seedling beside it.

proposal.direction: Pick the plastic out. Show the fourteen orange pieces gathered into one small heap at the corner of the beach, a line of footprints along the storm line leading to it, and the wrack line left clean.
proposal.rationale: Someone always walks the storm line in the morning; second attempt, and the room agreed that a beach that keeps everything should also show somebody clearing it.
